ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The diagram shows a two-stage transistor amplifier with VT1 as the first amplifier stage and VT2 as the second amplifier stage. The input signal ui is coupled through capacitor C5 into the base/input node of VT1. VT1 is coupled to VT2 through capacitor C1, and the output uo is taken from the VT2 collector side through capacitor C2. The resistor Rf is drawn along the bottom of the circuit, connecting the lower output/emitter-return region back to the VT1 input node. Reasoning: Topologically, Rf takes its feedback signal from the output current/return path, so the sampled output quantity is current. At the input side, Rf feeds the returned signal directly into the same node as the applied input signal, meaning the feedback is mixed in parallel, i.e. shunt mixing. The returned signal opposes the original input signal, so the feedback is negative. Therefore, Rf introduces current-shunt negative feedback.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: Rf is the bottom resistor linking the amplifier’s lower output/emitter-return node to the input junction at VT1 base, while the input source enters the same junction through C5. Imagine the output-stage current increasing; this changes the potential/current in the lower return node and drives a proportional feedback current through Rf into the input junction. Since the feedback quantity depends on output current, it is current feedback. Since it is summed as a current at the same input node as the source, it is shunt feedback. The direction of this returned current reduces the effective input drive, so the feedback is negative. Therefore Rf introduces current-shunt negative feedback.
